title: Random matrix discrepancy -- CLuP algorithm and parametric RDT approach
abstract: arXiv:2611.18650v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study information-theoretic and algorithmic aspects of random matrix discrepancy in proportional regime. The problem amounts to finding $\kappa=\min_{\x\in\mB^n}\|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bar{A}_i\x_i\|_2$, where $\bar{A}_i\in\mR^{d\times d}$ is a collection of $n$ iid GOE matrices, $\mB^n$ are vertices of the unit cube in $\mR^n$, and $\alpha=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\frac{n}{d^2}$ is a proportionality constant.   Strong progress is made in several directions: (i) We develop a Random duality theory (RDT) framework and utilize its a lifted variant to establish lower bounds on $\kappa$, which precisely match the bounds obtained via the first moment in [81]. (ii) To address analytical challenges, we propose a negative Hopfield model as a proxy for implementation of a fully lifted RDT. On the 2nd lifting level, this model fits remarkably well between the information-theoretic lower bounds from [81] and the algorithmic upper bounds from [38]. (i

translated_title: 随机矩阵偏差——CLuP算法与参数化RDT方法
translated_abstract: 我们研究了比例机制下随机矩阵偏差问题的信息论与算法层面。该问题等价于求解 $\kappa=\min_{\x\in\mB^n}\|\sum_{i=1}^{n}\bar{A}_i\x_i\|_2$，其中 $\bar{A}_i\in\mR^{d\times d}$ 是 $n$ 个独立同分布的GOE矩阵，$\mB^n$ 是 $\mR^n$ 中单位立方体的顶点，$\alpha=\lim_{n\rightarrow \infty}\frac{n}{d^2}$ 是比例常数。我们在多个方向上取得了重要进展：(i) 我们建立了随机对偶理论框架，并利用其提升变体建立了 $\kappa$ 的下界，该下界与文献[81]中通过第一矩方法得到的界精确吻合。(ii) 为应对分析上的挑战，我们提出负Hopfield模型作为完全提升RDT实现的代理。在第2提升层级上，该模型的结果在文献[81]的信息论下界与文献[38]的算法上界之间契合得非常良好。
tldr: 该论文建立了随机对偶理论（RDT）框架研究随机矩阵偏差问题，其提升变体得到的下界与第一矩方法精确匹配，并创新性地引入负Hopfield模型作为完全提升RDT的代理，其第二层级结果恰好落在信息论下界与算法上界之间。
en_tdlr: The paper develops a Random Duality Theory (RDT) framework whose lifted variant establishes lower bounds on random matrix discrepancy precisely matching first-moment bounds, and introduces a negative Hopfield model as a proxy for fully lifted RDT, whose 2nd lifting level fits remarkably well between the information-theoretic lower bounds and the algorithmic upper bounds.
